headline: $4.2B DONLIN DEAL — NovaGold Buys Paulson's 100% Stake; 39M-Oz Alaska Giant Consolidated, 520K Oz/Yr Attributable Upside
snippet: NovaGold Resources announced a US$4.2 billion all-stock transaction with Paulson Advisers on July 22 to consolidate 100% ownership of the Donlin Gold project in Alaska — one of the world's largest undeveloped gold deposits at 39+ million ounces — into a new Delaware entity called NovaGold Corporation, adding 520,000 ounces per year in attributable production over the first decade. Existing NovaGold shareholders receive one share of the new company for each share held, while Paulson holds approximately 35% of the new entity with voting power capped at 19.9%; deal closing is targeted for Q4 2026, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals.

headline: SILVER FOUR-DAY RALLY EYES $60 BREAKOUT — Sixth Consecutive Annual Deficit at 46.3M Oz Underpins Move; Highest Level in Three Weeks
snippet: Spot silver rose for a fourth consecutive session on July 22, trading as high as $60.55 per ounce as the $60 psychological level came firmly into focus — supported by escalating Middle East tensions and a structural supply deficit the Silver Institute confirmed at 46.3 million ounces in 2026, the sixth consecutive annual shortfall and the widest on record. The four-day run lifted silver from below $57 to its highest level in roughly three weeks, tracking gold's parallel safe-haven bid while drawing additional momentum from industrial demand running structurally above mined supply.

headline: WESTGOLD TOPS FY26 GUIDANCE AT 387,000 OZ — Treasury Swells to A$939M, $1.5B Liquidity; Q4 Cash Build A$233M (ASX: WGX)
snippet: Westgold Resources (ASX: WGX) released its June 2026 quarterly slides on July 22, reporting full-year FY26 gold production of 387,000 ounces at an all-in sustaining cost of A$2,841 per ounce — exceeding full-year guidance — while the company's treasury swelled to A$939 million with A$1.5 billion total liquidity including a A$600 million undrawn credit facility. Q4 production of approximately 99,000 ounces was sold at A$6,391 per ounce realized, generating a Q4 underlying cash build of A$233 million before buybacks and growth capital; full FY26 financial results plus FY27 guidance are scheduled for August.

headline: VANECK: 'MINERS ARE THE STANDOUT TRADE' — Gold's 25% Pullback Is Noise; Cash Flows, M&A Pipeline Point to Re-Rating
snippet: VanEck investment director Nik Casanova told Kitco News on July 22 that gold's 25% pullback from its January record is 'noise within the structural bull,' with the real opportunity in gold mining stocks — which he called 'the standout trade' — citing margins at multi-year highs, accelerating M&A across the sector, and operating leverage that will amplify returns when the gold price trajectory resumes. Casanova flagged junior miners in particular as undervalued relative to the underlying commodity, with many trading at significant discounts to NAV despite record gold prices boosting cash flow visibility across the sector.

headline: STONEX: FORGET IRAN — MID-4% YIELDS ARE THE REAL GOLD KILLER; Red Sea Blockade Creates Bid But Can't Overcome the Fed
snippet: StoneX precious metals analysts published a note on July 20 arguing that even as US military strikes on Iran enter their second week and Houthi rebels blockade Bab el-Mandeb, interest rates — not geopolitical risk — remain the primary price driver for gold and silver in 2026. With 10-year Treasury yields hovering in the mid-4% range under newly confirmed Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, StoneX sees continued headwinds for non-yielding metals despite the escalating war news, noting that gold and silver 'face downside risk' unless the Fed pivots materially on its rate path ahead of the July 29 FOMC decision.

headline: CALEDONIA Q2 GOLD +18% QoQ AS GRADE CLIMBS TO 3.05 g/t IN JULY — 72K-76.5K Oz FY26 Guidance Intact; 7-Day Week in Effect
snippet: Caledonia Mining (NYSE-A: CMCL) reported Q2 2026 gold production of 17,360 ounces from Zimbabwe's Blanket Mine — up 18% quarter-over-quarter from Q1's 14,767 ounces — as access to higher-grade mining areas improved, with the Q2 average grade of 2.88 g/t rising further to 3.05 g/t in July to date. The company reaffirmed its 2026 full-year guidance of 72,000 to 76,500 ounces and flagged H2-weighted production as a seven-day working week (implemented from June) and an upgraded elution plant expected to add roughly 200 tonnes per day of processing capacity through the back half of the year.

headline: PHYSICAL GOLD OR MINER ETF? — GLD Hedges the Fall, GDX Multiplies the Upside; But a 10% Gold Drop Wiped Out the Leveraged Gains
snippet: Motley Fool published a direct comparison of physical gold ETFs (GLD, IAU) versus gold mining stock ETFs (GDX, GDXJ) on July 21, concluding that physical gold protects capital with lower volatility during corrections while miners offer operating leverage that amplifies gains in rising markets — but brutally magnifies losses when the metal corrects. The article notes that gold's recent 10% monthly decline translated into a bloodbath across mining ETFs, erasing billions in market cap, and advises investors to choose based on risk tolerance: physical gold for capital preservation, miners only for those confident in a sustained price recovery.

headline: MOUNT POLLEY DRILLING RETURNS: 334m AT 0.24% CU — Imperial Metals Gets New Permit; Huckleberry Exploration Update Also Released (TSX: III)
snippet: Imperial Metals (TSX: III) reported on July 21 that drilling at Mount Polley Mine in British Columbia has returned two strong copper intercepts — hole MZ-26-08A cut 334.0 metres grading 0.24% copper plus 1.87 g/t silver, while hole MZ-26-07 returned 301.5 metres at 0.21% Cu — alongside confirmation that the mine has received a new operating permit, clearing a key regulatory milestone. The update also included a Q2 2026 production summary and exploration results from Huckleberry Mine, as Imperial advances multiple BC copper assets in a period of multi-year-high prices driven by tariff-related COMEX premiums and Chilean supply disruptions.

headline: STAR COPPER HITS PORPHYRY IN ALL FOUR 2026 HOLES — Star East, Star North, Copper Creek All Confirmed; Assays Pending (CSE: STCU)
snippet: Star Copper Corp. (CSE: STCU) announced on July 21 that all four of its first 2026 drill holes at the Star Porphyry Copper Project in British Columbia confirmed porphyry-style copper mineralization across three distinct targets — Star East, Star North, and the Copper Creek corridor — advancing the company's district-scale discovery thesis. Assays are pending for the initial holes, which were designed to test the lateral and vertical extent of the system at depth; the project sits along the same metallogenic belt hosting several of BC's major copper-molybdenum deposits, and is being advanced at a time when copper prices are testing multi-year highs near US$14,000 per tonne on the LME.
